chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Aban from al-Fadl ibn 'Abd al-Malik who said:
I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): Is the prayer offered over the deceased in the mosque? He said, 'Yes.'
From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them):

key_terms.يُصَلَّى: is prayed / is offered (passive verb referring to the funeral prayer)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to offer the funeral prayer for the deceased inside the mosque?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* confirms the permissibility of performing the funeral prayer (Salat al-Mayyit) within the mosque, a ruling that distinguishes Shia jurisprudence from some Sunni schools which may restrict it to the mosque courtyard or exclude it entirely. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of the Kufan scholars, particularly Al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik, in preserving this practical legal detail. This ruling underscores the mosque's role not just as a place of daily worship, but as a communal space for honoring the deceased and facilitating collective supplication.
